item.title: Ozu Castle and Cormorant Fishing — Guide
item.description: Ozu Castle stands above the Hiji River in the castle town of Ozu, sometimes called ‘little Kyoto’ for its old streets and riverside setting. Unusually, its four-storey wooden keep was faithfully reconstructed in the early 2000s using traditional methods and authentic materials, making it one of Japan’s most convincing modern wooden castle rebuilds — you can even stay overnight in the keep as a special experience. In summer, the river below comes alive with ukai, traditional cormorant fishing, in which fishermen in boats use trained cormorants to catch sweetfish by torchlight, a spectacle watched from pleasure boats.

item.title: Inuyama Cormorant Fishing: Firelit Nights on the Kiso River — Guide
item.description: Ukai, the ancient art of fishing with trained cormorants, has been practised on the Kiso River for some 1,300 years, and Inuyama’s summer performances unfold in one of its finest settings — the dark river beneath the floodlit silhouette of Japan’s oldest castle keep. From June to mid-October, spectators board wooden yakata boats hung with lanterns and drift alongside the fishing craft as usho masters in traditional grass skirts and ceremonial dress work a dozen leashed birds by the light of blazing pine-fire baskets, the flames, splashing and handlers' calls conjuring a scene unchanged for centuries.

item.title: Nagara River Ukai: 1,300 Years of Cormorant Fishing — Guide
item.description: Ukai, or cormorant fishing, on the Nagara River near Gifu City is one of Japan’s most spectacular living traditions, practised for roughly 1,300 years, in which master fishermen (usho) in traditional grass skirts guide trained cormorants to dive for ayu sweetfish by the light of blazing baskets of fire hung from their boats. Held on summer nights, the fishing is watched from passenger viewing boats that drift alongside, and the usho of the Nagara River even hold a special imperial appointment, underlining the cultural importance of this atmospheric nighttime spectacle.

item.title: Gifu Top Sightseeing: Shirakawa-go, Takayama & Cormorant Fishing
item.description: Gifu Prefecture occupies the mountainous heart of Honshu, a landlocked expanse of deep valleys, ancient cedar forests, and river gorges that stretches from the Northern Alps down to the Nobi Plain. It is a prefecture of genuine superlatives: one of Japan’s three great onsen towns, a UNESCO World Heritage village that looks unchanged from the eighteenth century, a mountain town preserved so completely that it earned the name Little Kyoto of the Alps, and a cormorant fishing tradition that has continued unbroken for thirteen hundred years.
